signals.name: processTokenCount
signals.quantity: number of times Parser#processToken() is invoked per test execution — with K self-referencing tokens each recursion level branches K times, yielding K^S total invocations where S is the recursion depth
signals.storage: ThreadLocal<long[]> in dosguide.agent.V1Counter (static field 'count', long[1] array to avoid boxing)
signals.reset: V1CostGradientGuidance.getInput() calls V1Counter.count.get()[0] = 0 before returning the InputStream
signals.read: V1CostGradientGuidance.handleResult() reads V1Counter.count.get()[0] and stores it; exported via lastSignals() as {"processTokenCount": N}

plans.retention: Primary: retain input if processTokenCount exceeds the running maximum (higher count means closer to timeout from exponential branching). Secondary (flat-signal, R46): when processTokenCount has not increased for 50 consecutive inputs, retain if the input's structural fingerprint is novel — fingerprint is computed from the count and byte-offsets of complete ${...} token boundaries in the input, so inputs with different token arrangements are explored even when signal is flat. Inputs that produce processTokenCount=0 (no tokens parsed) are never retained.
mutation: havoc: flip 1-4 random bits in the byte array (byte-level exploration)
byteInsert: insert 1-8 random bytes at a random position
byteDelete: delete 1-8 bytes from a random position
tokenRepeat: find an existing ${...} token boundary in the input and duplicate it (increases K, the branching factor — most important operator for V1)
tokenInsert: insert a complete ${CHANGES, format="%m"} (23 bytes) from the dictionary at a random position in the input
tokenCorrupt: pick a random byte inside a ${...} boundary and replace it with a random byte (explores near-valid token forms)
splice: given two retained inputs, take a random-length prefix of one and a random-length suffix of the other
dictReplace: replace a random 1-7 byte span with a dictionary token chosen at random from: ${, }, CHANGES, format, =, ", %m, comma, space, ${CHANGES, format="%m"}

tokenEncoder: structured operator that builds an input of exactly K copies of the full self-referencing token ${CHANGES, format="%m"} concatenated (23K bytes), where K is sampled 2..max_tokens based on budget — this is the primary encoder for constructing triggering inputs that pass the parser

signals.name: findNanos
signals.quantity: wall-clock nanoseconds spent inside the Matcher.find() call within BeginningOrEndMatchTransorm#transform — measures the backtracking cost of the regex engine on the user-controlled pattern and subject
signals.storage: ThreadLocal<long[]> in dosguide.agent.V2Counter (static fields 'findNanos' and 'startNanos', each long[1])
signals.reset: V2VulnDirectedGuidance.getInput() calls V2Counter.findNanos.get()[0] = 0 before returning the InputStream
signals.read: V2VulnDirectedGuidance.handleResult() reads V2Counter.findNanos.get()[0] and stores it; exported via lastSignals() as {"findNanos": N}

plans.retention: Primary: retain input if findNanos exceeds the running maximum (higher nanos means more backtracking, closer to timeout). Secondary (flat-signal, R46): when findNanos has not increased for 50 consecutive inputs, retain if the pattern portion (bytes before NUL) contains a novel combination of regex metacharacters or the subject portion (bytes after NUL) is longer than previously retained subjects. Inputs that throw PatternSyntaxException are discarded (they never reach the Matcher.find sink).
mutation: havoc: flip 1-4 random bits in the byte array (byte-level exploration)
byteInsert: insert 1-8 random bytes at a random position
byteDelete: delete 1-8 bytes from a random position
patternMutate: modify a random byte in the pattern portion (before the NUL separator), biased 70% toward regex metacharacters from dictionary: (, ), +, *, |, [, ], .
subjectExtend: append 1-20 copies of the character 'a' (0x61) to the subject portion (after NUL) — increases backtracking path length, most important operator for amplifying V2 signal
patternNest: find an existing (...) group in the pattern and wrap it in an additional quantified group, e.g. (X)+ becomes ((X)+)+ — increases ambiguity depth
alternationInsert: insert |<char> inside an existing parenthesized group in the pattern, creating ambiguous alternation that resists JDK 17 optimization (e.g., (a)+ becomes (a|aa)+)
separatorShift: move the NUL byte position left or right by 1-4 bytes to rebalance pattern vs subject lengths
crossover: combine the pattern portion (before NUL) of one retained input with the subject portion (after NUL) of another retained input

redosEncoder: structured operator that builds an input as pattern_bytes + NUL + N copies of 'a', where pattern_bytes is drawn from dictionary seeds like (a|aa)+b or (a|a)+b and N is sampled from a range scaled to budget — primary encoder for constructing well-formed ReDoS inputs that pass Pattern.compile
dictReplace: replace a random span in the pattern portion with a dictionary token chosen at random from: (, ), +, *, |, a, b, (a|aa)+b, (a|a)+
